Classifications of chief-of-mission positions made under the delegation are accrued consequences; the delegation itself ended with the revocation.
earlier_end_check: The order has no fixed end date. I examined the repeal of the 1946 Act by the Foreign Service Act of 1980: the repeal took effect February 15, 1981 (section 2403(a)), the same day as the revocation, and section 2401(a) kept orders issued under the 1946 Act in force until revoked, so it is not an earlier end. The dossier's chain also lists an acting record labeled EO 9452 dated 1944-06-26; that is a labeling artifact of the Federal Register issue that prints Executive Order 12292 (EO 9452 predates this order and cannot revoke it). No other revoking instrument appears in the three selected machine searches.
scope_check: One clause is inventoried: the whole order, a single delegation of the President's classification power for chief-of-mission positions plus its effective-date sentence. Executive Order 12292 section 10(b) revokes the order by number as a whole.
independent_command_check: The delegation depended on section 411 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946, now replaced by section 401 of the 1980 Act, which supplies its own classification power; the order contains no independent regulation or duty. savings_check: Executive Order 12292 was read at sections 2, 10 and 11; savings rest on section 2(c) of that order and sections 2401(a) and 2403(a) of the 1980 Act. Savings state transferred_or_accrued.
